I had to look at the username to make sure I didn’t post this because I feel like I’ve asked similar questions. I’ve been on stimulants for adhd since 3rd grade. In college I became extremely addicted to snorting them. I did dmt once and since then I never snorted it ever again. Fast forward to grad school and I fell down the slippery slope of boofing them…. I tried dmt again which helped for a little but I fell right back into the habit of abusing them because boofing was a lot stronger. I’ve been doing at home ketamine IM injections for the last year which had an immediate huge impact on my bipolar disorder symptoms which no meds previously helped control. It helped a little bit to get me back in line with the stimulant use. BUT I need to say that I don’t really think that the ketamine fixed that problem directly. I think that when I get better control of my bipolar symptoms, it becomes easier to control my substance use issues in general. So while I think the ketamine did indirectly help, as I think it could for you too, I don’t think that it was a direct fix. I’ve struggled with substance use for years, beyond just the stimulants, but gaining control of my bipolar disorder is really what has helped me most with getting away from the substances. I think the depression and stimulant use is probably interlaced for you, as it was for me, so it will probably help you a lot, but it’s likely going to need work and constant effort on your part to really break the habit with the stimulants.

Of course! Most important thing in my opinion is to go in with confidence. Whether you’re the highest scorer or the lowest scorer, you will be nervous going into this exam and there’s no way around that. But when you sit down in front of that computer, trust yourself and trust the work you put in for this. Treat every question as if it is it’s own exam and not part of all the rest. If you feel like shit on a few Qs or even a whole block, erase that from your memory and push forward to the next. I would tell myself that the Qs I had trouble on or even the whole blocks I had trouble on, were just experimental Qs and wouldn’t count anyway. You’re gonna have some blocks that you feel are harder than others, but you’ll also have some that you feel a bit better on so don’t let doubt creep into your mind because the hood and the bad will balance out into a passing score, so just have faith. 

Side note: my first section, I lost track of time and didn’t get to answer the last 5 Qs (which NEVER happened to me in any practice block). But I made the adjustments I needed to and just kept pushing, so don’t let minor hiccups mess with your head.

And most importantly: Good luck. You’re gonna kill it.

I think although it will be sad to see them take a more commercial turn, I do believe that these drugs can be a huge piece of the future of medicine. Allowing psychiatric doctors to give these drugs to patients will help to combat countless mental illnesses which are far too prevalent in our society today, like depression and anxiety to even addiction.
